question: How many schedules are there in the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: VII
VI
IV
V
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is IV

Explanation:
The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 of India contains four schedules. These schedules provide varying degrees of protection to different species. Schedule I includes endangered species that receive absolute protection. Schedule II includes specially protected animals whose hunting is prohibited but may be allowed under certain conditions. Schedule III and IV include less protected species with regulated hunting. The Act originally had 6 schedules, but amendments reduced it to 4 schedules currently in force. The schedules classify species based on the level of protection required, with Schedule I offering the highest level of protection.

☛ What type of species are included in Schedule I? → Endangered species
☛ Which schedule provides absolute protection? → Schedule I
☛ What is the provision of Schedule II? → Specially protected animals
☛ What do Schedule III and IV contain? → Less protected species

question: Which public sector enterprise has the status of Maharatna? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Indian Oil Corporation Limited

Explanation:
Maharatna status is the highest category granted to Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) by the Government of India. This status is awarded to PSUs that have a significant global presence and annual profits exceeding ₹5,000 crore. Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) is India's largest oil and gas company and holds Maharatna status. question: Name the monument which is a testimony to successful restoration and preservation of an archaeological site. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Sanchi Stupa
Palika Bazaar
Gateway of India
India Gate
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sanchi Stupa

Explanation:
The Sanchi Stupa, located in Madhya Pradesh, is a famous Buddhist monument built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. It is renowned for its successful restoration and preservation. In the 19th century, British archaeologists and later the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) undertook conservation work. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989. The architecture and sculptures at Sanchi represent the history of Buddhism. The site is a testimony to successful restoration because its original structure and artifacts have been well-preserved, reflecting the efforts to maintain its authenticity and integrity.

question: Which of the United Nation's organization has the International Institute of Educational Planning at Paris as its Part? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/01/2021) Shift 1)

question: What is the full form of WCED (also known as Brundtland Commission) formed by the United Nations for sustainable development? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: World Commission on Ecological Development
World Commission on Environment and Development
World Commission on Environmental Delegation
World Commission on Educational Development
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is World Commission on Environment and Development

Explanation:
The full form of WCED is World Commission on Environment and Development. It was established by the United Nations in 1983 to address sustainable development issues. The commission was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland, then Prime Minister of Norway, hence it is commonly known as the Brundtland Commission. In 1987, the commission published the report 'Our Common Future', which defined sustainable development as 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs'. The commission focused on balancing environmental protection with economic development.

question: Name the space shuttle in which Kalpana Chawla, an Indian-American astronaut, died in 2003. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Columbia
Discovery
Challenger
Atlantis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Columbia

Explanation:
Indian-American astronaut Kalpana Chawla died in the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster on February 1, 2003, during the STS-107 mission. The shuttle disintegrated upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere, killing all seven crew members. Columbia was the first reusable space shuttle, first launched in 1981. The accident led to major safety improvements in NASA's Space Shuttle program. Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin in space, having previously flown on STS-87 in 1997.

question: Which one of the following bodies are NOT Bretton Woods Institutions?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (16/02/2021) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following is NOT an economic grouping formed by different nations to strengthen their economies? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 1)

question: Which freedom fighter is remembered for his efforts in achieving the official language of India as Hindi? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (17/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Munishwar Dutt Upadhyay
Mahavir Tyagi
Purushottam Das Tandon
Ram Manohar Lohia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Purushottam Das Tandon

Explanation:
Purushottam Das Tandon, known as the 'Father of Hindi', played a pivotal role in making Hindi the official language of India. He was the president of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan in 1948 and strongly advocated for Hindi as the national language in the Constituent Assembly. He believed Hindi could unify the diverse linguistic groups of India. His efforts culminated in the adoption of Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union under the Constitution of India in 1950. Tandon also served as the president of the Indian National Congress. His relentless work for Hindi earned him the title 'Rajarshi'. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1961 for his contributions to public service and language.

question: After the signing of which treaty did the European Community come to be known as the European Union? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (27/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: The Treaty of Lisbon, 2007
The Single European Act, 1986
The Treaty of Maastricht, 1992
The Treaty of Amsterdam, 1997
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Treaty of Maastricht, 1992

Explanation:
The Treaty of Maastricht, also known as the Treaty on European Union, was signed on 7 February 1992 and came into force on 1 November 1993. It transformed the European Economic Community (EEC) into the European Union (EU). The treaty established the three-pillar structure: the European Communities, Common Foreign and Security Policy, and Justice and Home Affairs. It laid the groundwork for the euro currency and introduced the concept of EU citizenship. The treaty also increased the powers of the European Parliament.
